ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right triangle $\triangle ABC$, the height $AD=4$ on the hypotenuse $BC$, and $\cos B =\frac{4}{5}$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given in right triangle $ABC$, $AD \perp BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD + \angle B = \angle BAD + \angle DAC = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle B = \angle DAC$,\\
Since $\cos B = \frac{4}{5}$,\\
$\therefore \cos \angle DAC = \frac{AD}{AC} = \frac{4}{5}$,\\
Given that $AD = 4$,\\
$\therefore AC = \boxed{5}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: B, D, C are collinear on the bottom segment BC, A is above D, and AD is drawn perpendicular to BC with a right-angle marker at D; AB and AC form the two legs of the larger right triangle, with BC as the hypotenuse. From the text, use AD = 4 and cos B = 4/5, and note that ABC is right-angled with altitude AD to the hypotenuse. Use complementary-angle/altitude geometry: since AD ⟂ BC, triangle ABD is right at D, so angle B is complementary to angle BAD. Since triangle ABC is right at A, angle DAC is also complementary to angle BAD. Therefore angle B = angle DAC. Then transfer the cosine value: cos(angle DAC) = cos B = 4/5. In right triangle ADC, cos(angle DAC) = AD/AC, so 4/AC = 4/5, giving AC = 5.
